agent_answered.text: "Good push, and I'd put it inside step 1, because "who can read the bytes" really means "who can ever hold the key". The uncomfortable part is that per-item or per-period keys mostly help against a leak of a *current* key, not of whatever unlocks the archive. If the user still needs to open last year's notes, something on their device can still derive or unwrap last year's key, so a ... en stay under the old key. Where per-period keys do earn their keep is sharing: a share link with its own key limits a leaked link to that one item, which is a slice in the sense you mean." [c494d43c]
